Sports.title: Leeds reach £34m agreement on Bosnia star, Man United seal £35m Youri Tielemans deal... and Arsenal eye Greece forward after Leandro Trossard seals £17m exit: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Leeds reach £34m agreement on Bosnia star, Man United seal £35m Youri Tielemans deal... and Arsenal eye Greece forward after Leandro Trossard seals £17m exit: WINDOW WATCH

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Leeds close to £34m Tarik

Leeds have reached a provisional agreement on a £34m fee with Sassuolo for 23-year-old Bosnia international Tarik Muharemovic.

The Italian club had said earlier that talks were advancing for the centre back.

Juventus will receive 50percent of any fee so stand to receive £17m.

Tarik Muharemovic was on the end of this tackle from Folarin Balogun - for which the USA forward received a red card for but saw his ban suspended after Donald Trump intervened

Arsenal still in for Alvarez

Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez remains an option for Arsenal.

The Argentina forward would prefer to join Barcelona if they can reach agreement with Atletico but that relationship remains strained.

Arsenal are monitoring developments in case the opportunity to sign the 26-year-old opens up. Atletico have dismissed offers of £100m.

Two suitors for Rangers' Souttar

Leicester City and Sheffield United are showing interest in Rangers defender John Souttar.

The 29-year-old signed a new one-year deal at Rangers in February but did not travel to the club’s pre-season training camp in Spain, with Brazilian striker Danilo also staying at home.

John Souttar was one of three Rangers players at the World Cup with Scotland

Leeds want another keeper with Torino keen on Perri

Torino are pushing to sign Leeds United goalkeeper Lucas Perri but need the Elland Road side to sign another keeper first.

Leeds have seen out-of-contract Illan Meslier join Arsenal and Karl Darlow join Manchester United.

They have handed a new deal to Alex Cairns but are continuing to look for a new No1. Talks have taken place with Parma for Zion Suzuki but other options are also being explored.

Leeds remain in talks with Sassuolo over centre back Tarik Muharemovic and Southampton over Shea Charles. But, again, they have alternatives.

Tielemans proud to join United

Manchester United's midfield overhaul has moved on with the £35million signing of Youri Tielemans. The 29-year-old Belgian, who has joined from Aston Villa after his release clause was triggered, has signed a five-year deal at Old Trafford.

Tielemans said: 'It's hard to describe just how proud I am to join Manchester United.

'Signing for such a special club feels incredible, it is the culmination of years of dedication since I first fell in love with football.'

Click HERE to read more

Youri Tielemans has sealed his move to Old Trafford on a five-year deal

Arsenal ready for Tzolis bid after Trossard exit

Bruges are anticipating a bid from Arsenal for Christos Tzolis now that Leandro Trossard is confirmed as heading to Besiktas.

The Greece forward is keen on the move after seeing previous offers from the Premier League rejected, notably Crystal Palace.

The 24-year-old former Norwich winger also has interest from elsewhere but is set on Arsenal if they can agree a fee.

Christos Tzolis in action against Arsenal in last season's Champions League

Aberdeen head Feeney interest

Aberdeen head a list of clubs interested in Carlisle defender Morgan Feeney, 27, the club’s captain and player of the year signed by former boss Mark Hughes who has one year left on his contract.

The club’s American owners, who sacked Hughes, are yet to offer Feeney new terms.

JIM FOULERTON

Trossard completes £17m move to Turkey

Leandro Trossard has joined Besiktas from Arsenal in a deal worth £17million

Leandro Trossard has joined Besiktas from Arsenal in a deal worth £17m.

The Belgian winger departs the Premier League champions in a deal worth an initial £15.3m plus £1.7m in add-ons.

Trossard played a crucial role for Mikel Arteta playing 174 times in three-and-a-half years, scoring 36 goals.

During Arsenal's title-winning campaign last term, Trossard scored eight goals and registered 11 assists in 50 matches in all competitions.

Arsenal have been talking to Bruges over a deal for Christos Tzolis among other targets.

Leeds United are bringing in Cardiff City head analyst Matthew Jenkins who had been at the club for eight years.

City contemplating Bouaddi move

Manchester City are continuing to assess the figures being demanded by Lille for midfield prodigy Ayyoub Bouaddi.

As Daily Mail Sport have reported, City have retained a long-standing interest in the teenage Morocco international and want to bring in another midfielder alongside Elliot Anderson with long-term concerns over Rodri, who has still to agree a new contract.

Nico Gonzalez could be sold while Tijjani Reijnders, who had tentative interest from Atletico Madrid, could also go.

Bouaddi's performances have seen his value rise above £60m which was considered his asking price before the World Cup.

Manchester City have long held interest in Morocco star Ayyoub Bouaddi

Lille ideally wanted him to stay another season on loan as part of the deal but negotiations are open.

Meanwhile, Stade Brestois are among clubs showing interest in City defender Juma Bah who was on loan at Nice last season.

The 20-year-old, 6ft 5ins centre back could be among the players figuring in a showcase game at City today.

Darlow deal done

Manchester United have completed the signing of goalkeeper Karl Darlow.

The Wales international joins on a free transfer after his contract expired at Leeds.

Darlow finished last season as Leeds' number one and kept five clean sheets. They wanted to re-sign him while Everton and Tottenham also held talks.

Former Leeds goalkeeper Karl Darlow has made the move to Old rafford

Bristol City hope for Ballard compromise

Bristol City are working to find a compromise with Leyton Orient over a fee for striker Dom Ballard.

The 21-year-old, who scored 23 goals in League One last season, is set on a move to Ashton Gate but so far they have been unable to agree a deal with Orient who have been pushing for over £5million.

Southampton are also due sell-on percentage for the striker who, at the 2026 EFL Awards, was named in the League One Team of the Season, Player of the Season and Young Player of the Season.

Mason Greenwood set for Turkey

Mason Greenwood is to be confirmed as a new Fenerbahce player in a £34million deal

Mason Greenwood is to be confirmed as a new Fenerbahce player after they agreed a permanent deal with Marseille of around £34million.

Manchester United are due 40 per cent of the overall fee, although 20 per cent of that will go to Getafe, who took Greenwood on loan for the 2023-24 season.

As previously reported, that should work out around £10.2million.

Villa defender heading for Spain loan spell

Aston Villa right back Andres Garcia is closing on a loan move to Getafe.

The 23-year-old joined Villa from Levante 18 months ago in a £6million deal but made only 8 appearances last season.

Villa are looking to juggle a number of transfers this window to meet UEFA financial requirements.

They still want to strengthen after agreeing to sign Johan Manzambi from Freiburg but are losing Youri Tielemans to Manchester United for £36m and Lucas Digne to Paris St Germain for £8.5m.

There is also interest around Ollie Watkins and while they don't want to lose Morgan Rogers, offers from Arsenal are anticipated.

Sunderland land Thomas Menuier

Sunderland are signing Thomas Meunier on a two year contract.

The Belgium international, who was part of their World Cup squad, is a free agent after leaving Lille and has been talking to Valencia.

Hull City had also opened discussions with the 34-year-old right back but he has travelled to the North East this morning to complete a medical and sign for Sunderland.

Sunderland are signing Belgian international Thomas Meunier on a two year contract

Roma pressing for Garnacho

Roma are continuing to press for Chelsea misfit Alejandro Garnacho.

The Argentine has been granted permission to seek a new club and is not in Xabi Alonso's plans.

Chelsea want £40m and a permanent sale as Manchester United also retain a sell-on clause.

Roma are continuing to press for Chelsea misfit Alejandro Garnacho

Roma enquired a week ago and their latest proposal is for an initial loan with an option to buy for around £30m. It would become an obligation if certain conditions are met and the loan would carry a fee of £4.3m.

Chelsea maintain they want a guaranteed sale.

Chelsea are also looking to move on Axel Disasi, Benoit Badiashile and Filip Jorgensen. Mamadou Sarr could leave on loan amid Premier League interest.

Vuskovic leaves Spurs for Brighton

Luka Vuskovic has completed his move from Tottenham to Brighton for £46million plus £4m achievable add-ons.

Spurs have secured a 20 per cent sell-on clause for the Croatia international and buy-back matching rights.

Vuskovic and his representatives made clear his desire to play regular first team football in the season ahead and did not want another loan.

The 19-year-old centre half has had three separate loans since Spurs struck a deal to sign him from Hajduk Split for £12m.

Last season at Hamburg was a huge success but Roberto De Zerbi was unable to offer the guarantee of regular first team football at Spurs.

Luka Vuskovic has completed his move from Tottenham to Brighton for £46million plus £4m achievable add-ons

De Zerbi has reinforced in central defence with Marcos Senesi and Jan Paul van Hecke, who they signed from Brighton for £52m.

So, Spurs will bank a huge profit on a young player who never made a competitive appearance for them and whose wages they have never paid.

Only Harry Kane and Kyle Walker have been sold by Spurs for bigger fees in the last 10 years.

MATT BARLOW

Man City host showcase game for fringe stars

Manchester City host a showcase game today for the benefit of their fringe players.

Around 90 clubs are expected to be represented in the stands after they were invited to attend the game and view potential loan or permanent buy targets.

City players such as Preston North End target Divin Mubama, Matty Warhurst, Jaden Heskey, Claudio Echeverri, Spike Brits and Charlie Gray are all due to play a part as clubs from the UK and abroad come to take a close look.

A number of guest players from other clubs within City Football Group who are looking to move on have also been invited to take part. Stredair Appuah and Kris Lund from Palermo plus Amar Fatah and Elijah Odede from Troyes.

City have also scheduled a further showcase game against Salford City on August 4.

Sports.title: Harry Brook brands Brendon McCullum sacking 'disappointing' as his England one-day side slump to heavy defeat by India
Sports.content:
Brendon McCullum’s coaching career might have taken a new twist but he was confronted with a familiar failing in Birmingham as his one-day side slumped to a heavy defeat by India.

It has been, to say the least, a rollercoaster few days. On Saturday, his T20 side went top of the world rankings after completing a 4–0 hammering of the Indians in Southampton. On Sunday, England announced he had been sacked as Test coach. On Monday, he apologised to fans for the team’s failings.

Tuesday? That was just another 50-over defeat, this time by six wickets with 28 balls to spare, as India captain Shubman Gill followed his epic double of 269 and 161 here in last summer’s Test by scoring 80 off 75 balls before retiring hurt with cramp.

And it left white-ball captain Harry Brook reflecting not just on another one-day defeat, England’s 20th out of 30 since the end of the 2023 World Cup, but also on the coach’s change of circumstance.

‘It was disappointing for me,’ he said of McCullum’s sacking. ‘He’s played a massive part in my career, and he’s been awesome for me. He’s going to be missed.’

Did the players feel they had let their coach down? ‘There’s always that sense of letting yourself down,’ said Brook. ‘But you’re in the results business and we expect to win games of cricket.’

Harry Brook (right) has said he is 'disappointed' by Brendon McCullum's (left) Test sacking

The duo will continue to work together with England's white ball sides but their one-day team suffered a heavy defeat by India on Tuesday

English hopes briefly lifted when Gill’s retirement was followed by the run-out of Shreyas Iyer by Brook’s direct hit from midwicket, and the dismissal of KL Rahul, chopping on against Josh Tongue.

Virat Kohli had already gone for just five, trapped by Jofra Archer as he aimed across the line, and at 160 for four the tourists were still 99 short of victory, with Gill’s involvement uncertain and the Indian tail consisting of three No 11s.

But the spin-bowling all-rounders Washington Sundar and Axar Patel held their nerve, to take a 1–0 lead in this three-match series ahead of Thursday’s second game in Cardiff.

Fast bowler Brydon Carse will be available again, having recovered from a hand and wrist injury that has ruled him out of international cricket since the Ashes, but England will need more than one new addition to transform their fortunes.

As electric as their recent T20 cricket has been, they remain also-rans in the 50-over format, and a lowly eighth in the rankings, having never come close to touching the heights they attained when they were crowned world champions in 2019. McCullum’s pre-match suggestion that they can challenge for the title next year in southern Africa sounded like one of the more outlandish claims made during the Bazball era.

It could have been worse. When Will Jacks was brilliantly caught low to his right by Rahul behind the stumps off Shivam Dube, England had somehow slipped from 61 without loss to 107 for six after choosing to make first use of a decent Edgbaston pitch.

Their collapse included Brook, who was caught at slip for a single from the first ball of a new spell by Jasprit Bumrah, before England earned a breather during a fighting seventh-wicket stand of 121 between Root and Liam Dawson, whose resourceful 68 was the highest score of his international career.

But thoughtless batting by the lower order left Root stranded on a run-a-ball 76, with 13 balls of the innings unused. It was enough to restore his ODI average to 50 for the first time in four years, even while the passage of play typified the carelessness that has become characteristic of England’s 50-over cricket.

Archer slogged to deep midwicket, Adil Rashid was stumped charging at Axar Patel, who then bowled Tongue to finish with four wickets. His unbeaten 57 in the evening sunshine confirmed him as the runaway player of the match.

Sports.title: Man United's £50m move for Andrey Santos unpacked: Why Brazilian was keen to leave Chelsea, the qualities he'll bring to Old Trafford - and why both Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior grew frustrated with him
Sports.content:
Man United's £50m move for Andrey Santos unpacked: Why Brazilian was keen to leave Chelsea, the qualities he'll bring to Old Trafford - and why both Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior grew frustrated with him

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Grateful for the vacancy at Manchester United, Andrey Santos leaves Chelsea after concluding the midfield had become too crowded for him.

Moises Caicedo’s new deal underlined his status in the starting line-up. Enzo Fernandez will only be allowed to leave if his club are offered £120million.

Reece James is another option in the middle, along with Romeo Lavia and Dario Essugo, both of whom are expected to stay unless a surprise market opens up for a pair whose last campaigns were disrupted by fitness problems.

Chelsea’s interest in Granit Xhaka tells us they are still in the market for more, and that is before getting to the Cobham prospects.

Santos did not mind spending a season as an understudy while the club were competing in the Champions League. But now they were facing a campaign without Europe entirely, the 22-year-old Brazilian requested talks to discuss him departing out of a desire for more meaningful minutes.

Chelsea sympathised, agreed, and, several weeks ago, gave his representatives Sports Invest UK permission to start canvassing potential suitors.

Andrey Santos with his wife Yngryd at his official Manchester United unveiling this week

United have spent £48million plus £2m in add-ons on Santos, bringing an end to the 22-year-old's three years at Chelsea

Evidently, no limitations were placed on where he could and could not go, with a domestic rival in United securing this tidy midfielder for the relatively sensible sum of £50million.

For Chelsea, that is worth £48m up front with £2m in achievable add-ons and 10 per cent of any future sale. It is a significant profit on the £16m fee they paid to Vasco da Gama in 2023.

However, a few fans around Stamford Bridge are not happy.

They do not blame Santos for wanting to leave, but they do think they should have extracted more money out of United because they see his potential.

United are not signing the completed package, but rather what Santos could become, and time on the pitch should hopefully aid his progress.

Chelsea had chances to sell Santos before. Last summer, they turned down a £45m approach from West Ham. United were sniffing around then, too. But Chelsea liked what they were seeing in flashes.

The passes played forwards, including the first-time ones around the corner which created chances and showed his eye. The willingness to defend, and the duels won. Enzo Maresca told us last August that he wanted Santos to stay as a midfield option, and so he did.

Then Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca wasn't happy after Santos' mistake led to Trevoh Chalobah being sent off with the Blues 1-0 up against Brighton, a game they went on to lose 3-1

Chelsea admired Santos' intent to play passes forward and his willingness to defend

Yet the last season was not too smooth for Santos, who was at fault on more than one occasion as Chelsea went from being talked up as title contenders to finishing 10th in the Premier League.

In September, when Chelsea hosted Brighton, Santos received a pass while filling in for James as the captain received treatment on the sidelines. Santos’ first touch was terrible, sending him backwards and allowing Kaoru Mitoma to press him aggressively. Santos desperately slid towards the ball in a bid to send it towards Robert Sanchez or Trevoh Chalobah. Instead, he gave it to Diego Gomez, and Chalobah brought him down before receiving a red card for denying a goalscoring opportunity.

Chelsea were winning 1-0 at the time of Chalobah’s dismissal. Down to 10 men, they ended up falling to a 3-1 defeat. Maresca was not pleased with Chalobah or Santos.

Absent from Chelsea’s next two games, Santos then started away at Nottingham Forest, only to be hooked at half-time as Maresca’s side were goalless. They went on to win 3-0. From then on, Maresca only handed starts to Santos in the less glamourous games, such as Qarabag away in the Champions League, Wolves away in the Premier League and Cardiff away in the Carabao Cup.

After Maresca's exit, Liam Rosenior’s arrival was supposed to spark something in Santos. He had thrived under him at Strasbourg, and Rosenior described Santos as tactically excellent when we asked for his take. Initially, Santos was a big winner of that appointment. The starts came one after another.

Then arrived Chelsea versus Burnley in February. Rosenior revealed afterwards how one of his players failed to fulfil their marking assignment as the visitors’ 6ft 1in striker Zian Flemming scored a free header in stoppage time to secure a 1-1 draw. Rosenior would not confirm who that culprit was. When the away side won another corner a minute later, however, it was suddenly Santos who was marking Flemming.

Even Rosenior seemed to lose trust in Santos as time wore on. Maybe we should not read too much into that, of course. The only players who impressed on Rosenior’s watch were Joao Pedro and Jorrel Hato.

But it felt telling that the footballer he knew better than everyone else was being benched. Santos was an unused substitute for Rosenior's final two games in charge.

Last season wasn't smooth for Santos, who was named in Brazil's preliminary squad for the World Cup but didn't make the final cut

Santos with United director of football Jason Wilcox - it's time for him to seize his opportunity and make Chelsea regret selling him

With Calum McFarlane taking over as interim head coach, one of Santos’ final starts in a Chelsea shirt arrived in April when Manchester City visited.

With Fernandez suspended, he stepped in, but was the one who was supposed to be marking Nico O’Reilly when he headed in to hand City their decisive lead. A big moment and a big mistake.

So there is room for improvement, but then United know that. He is young, talented, and has more experience than many other 22-year-olds. If Chelsea are to regret selling Santos, though, it is over to the Brazilian to step up and seize this opportunity at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Man United confirm £35m Youri Tielemans move as Michael Carrick lands third signing of the summer as part of squad rebuild
Sports.content:
Manchester United's midfield overhaul took another giant step towards completion with the £35million signing of Youri Tielemans.

The Belgian, who has joined from Aston Villa after his release clause was triggered, has signed a five-year deal at Old Trafford.

Tielemans said: 'It's hard to describe just how proud I am to join Manchester United.

'Signing for such a special club feels incredible, it is the culmination of years of dedication since I first fell in love with football.

'I have had the privilege of experiencing success in the game and it has only increased my determination to achieve more. The ambition from everyone at the club is extremely clear; we are all determined to push for the biggest trophies over the coming years.'

Youri Tielemans has joined Manchester United to become their third signing of the summer

Tielemans has signed a five-year contract after joining from Aston Villa this week

The move comes hours after United confirmed the signing of free agent goalkeeper Karl Darlow, who joined after a fine season at Leeds United in 2025-26, and a day after Andrey Santos arrived from Chelsea for £48million.

Director of football Jason Wilcox added: 'Youri has consistently been one of the most outstanding midfielders in the Premier League throughout the past seven years. He has all of the technical qualities, as well as the ambition and mentality, to thrive at Manchester United.

'Youri's consistency is exceptional, and he will add further composure, creativity and leadership to our squad.

'We are delighted to welcome a player of his influence and experience, both on the pitch and within the dressing room, as we continue to build a team ready to challenge for the biggest honours.'

Midfield has been the key area of focus for Michael Carrick and United's hierarchy this summer following the exit of Casemiro and the serious injury Manuel Ugarte sustained at the World Cup with Uruguay.

Ederson looked set to arrive from Atalanta but that deal collapsed following an extensive second medical and United have pivoted quickly to get two deals over the line for Santos and Tielemans.

Santos, 22, has signed a five-year contract until June 2031 with the option to extend it by another year.

The young Brazilian, who cost Chelsea £18m from Vasco Da Gama in January 2023, said: 'Everything about Manchester United is special; it is an incredible feeling to join a club that some of my biggest idols have represented.

'As a midfielder, I am really excited to have the opportunity to learn from Michael Carrick, he is the perfect coach to help me take the next step in my career and push to achieve my dreams.

'Everybody told me about how ambitious the club is and the amazing environment that has been created here. I know just how strong the squad is and I cannot wait to fight together to compete for the biggest trophies.'

Man United confirmed the signing of 22-year-old Brazilian Andrey Santos from Chelsea

Manchester United have made goalkeeper Karl Darlow their second signing of the summer

United's director of football Jason Wilcox said of Santos: 'Andrey is an outstanding midfielder with excellent technical qualities and the ability to impact the game at both ends of the pitch.

'He was a key target for us in an important position, so we are delighted that he will join Michael's squad so early in pre-season.

'Despite already having extensive experience, leadership abilities and proving his talent at the highest level, Andrey still has enormous potential to develop further, and we cannot wait to see him flourish at Manchester United.'

Sports.title: Liverpool 'could save millions with Arne Slot contract agreement' as Reds pave the way for former coach to become Netherlands boss
Sports.content:
Liverpool are reportedly set to benefit financially after reaching an agreement which paves the way for their former boss Arne Slot to be named Netherlands manager.

Slot was sacked by Liverpool at the end of May, just one year after the Dutchman had led the Reds to the Premier League title.

His dismissal came after Liverpool finished fifth in the Premier League at the end of a campaign where Slot oversaw 20 defeats in all competitions.

Slot also came under pressure from supporters and saw several key players - such as the now-departed Mohamed Salah - speak out about the playing style.

Liverpool have since appointed Andoni Iraola as Slot's successor, while the Dutchman has emerged as the leading candidate to succeed Ronald Koeman as Netherlands boss.

According to Dutch newspaper De Telegraaf, Slot's potential appointment is moving closer with Liverpool open to contributing to his salary.

Liverpool could top up Arne Slot's pay to help him become Netherlands boss, while reducing the compensation package due to their former boss

Slot is favourite to become Netherlands boss following the resignation of Ronald Koeman, pictured

Slot would have been entitled to a significant compensation package from Liverpool after his dismissal, with clubs tending to place coaches on gardening leave following their sacking.

The report claims Liverpool are prepared to top up Slot's salary in the first year with the national team, ensuring he is paid the full amount he was owed during the final year of his contract at Liverpool.

The agreement would ultimately lead to Liverpool paying out a smaller overall compensation package, while helping the Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB) to appoint Slot.

It is claimed Slot would have been due around £6.9m in compensation from Liverpool.

Slot was sacked following a review into Liverpool’s troubled season that was led by Richard Hughes and Michael Edwards, chief executive of football at the club’s owner, Fenway Sports Group.

Edwards has since quit the club with the 47-year-old's departure confirmed this week, one year before his contract had been due to end.

The KNVB have been looking for a new head coach following Koeman's resignation after the Netherlands' last-32 exit at the World Cup.

The Netherlands were beaten on penalties by Morocco after a 1-1 draw.

Koeman said he made the decision immediately after the Dutch's early exit from the tournament in North America. It brought to an end his second spell in charge of the national team, a role he also held from 2018 to 2020.

Sports.title: Dan Burn is England's viral sensation of this World Cup - but even he doesn't want to come on against Argentina!
Sports.content:
Dan Burn is England's viral sensation of this World Cup - but even he doesn't want to come on against Argentina!

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The clips flooded Dan Burn's phone. A viral sensation for the second time in a week, thundering through a former Brighton team-mate as the seconds ticked down in Miami, with England holding firm amid a Norwegian assault.

Burn's header flies out of play. He punches the air with both arms, stepping over his opponent as if retreating from a ruck. It typifies the grit instilled in this team by Thomas Tuchel and speaks to a squad that has embraced modern football while also maintaining English traditions.

'I used to play with Leo (Ostigard), the guy who I end up clattering with the header,' Burn says.

'I didn't really know what I'd done in the moment. I watched back and I thought, "Oh, it's not great," so I texted Leo after and just said, "Mate, I didn't mean to be disrespectful, I was just like fired up," and he was like, "Yeah, I get that, it's no problem."

'When that ball's in the air, my eyes lit up a little bit and I just wanted to go for it and do my part for the team.'

He has done that and more, wearing the Raul Jimenez bicycle kick on the nose in the humidity of the Azteca and heading another clearance 50 yards. Big Dan Burn has become an icon for plenty - and many taking a passing interest in the sport for the first time.

Dan Burn has become England's viral sensation of the 2026 World Cup in North America

Tuchel was clear with Burn what his role would be here. Closing games out. He readily accepted the opportunity. It is one that at 34 he now relishes but admits would have been harder to swallow in his earlier years.

'It's a tough one,' Burn adds while looking ahead to Wednesday's semi-final with Argentina, expected to be a physical tussle. 'Because really, you kind of do not want to have to come on at all and we'll win the World Cup.

'It's a hard one, mentally, because the best-case scenario for the team is that I'm not needed at all, but that also means that I don't get on the pitch.

'It's one of those where, if the game's tight at the end (against Norway), I'm warming up pretty much the entire second half, knowing that I was going to have to come on and do something — I just want to come on and do what I'm good at.'

Burn believes the identity of English football has been blended nicely and contributes to more success. And he recognises where he sits within that.

'I think it has probably changed over the last like 20 odd years. We're producing more what European football teams have been doing, like Spain and France.

'I feel like it used to be very different, but now the players that we're bringing through are at the same level as those countries.

Burn has played a key role in closing out England's last two wins over Mexcio and Norway

'Using Spain as an example, they're a lot more of a possession-based team because of the players that they have. Whereas we're probably a lot better at the counter-attack with the speed that we've got and the players that we've got going forward.

'Everyone's got their own style, but I think it has probably changed over the years since we're consistently making semi-finals.

'At Darlington, I can't say I ever dreamt of being in a World Cup semi-final, because it was so far off the radar. I felt like once I played in the Premier League, I'll be content. Or once I've played in the Champions League, I'll be content. Or once I've won a cup at Newcastle.

'You realise that you always want more. The amount of times I've thought about winning a cup at Newcastle and actually it was a bit of an anti-climax when you got there. You're just always wanted to get there.

'Now, dreaming of winning the World Cup, it's all of these bits leading up to it that will be the bits that you remember, not the actual (thing).'

So these days are to be cherished, the build-up, the brotherhood that Burn speaks so passionately about. The anticipation of what is to come.

But Burn is left hoping he won't be needed alongside Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane against Argentina

England are aware of the historical magnitude of this date with Argentina in Atlanta. It has become something of a diplomatic hot potato in the days before kick off.

Burn fell for football while watching the famous group stage victory in 2002, the David Beckham redemption, in the Cricketers' Arms when on holiday in Orlando as a 10-year-old. The Irish bar next to Universal is no longer with us, replaced by a whiskey joint.

'It must have been on quite late because I think it was just me and my dad,' Burn says. 'I think that was the sort of time when I fell in love with football.'

Beckham visited camp last week to receive his legacy cap from current skipper Harry Kane. 'I was bit starstruck, to be honest,' he admits. 'I rarely get starstruck now. I feel like when I meet people, I'm normally pretty cool. But I was like, 'f*** me, that's David Beckham'.'

Someone might be saying the same thing about Burn one of these days. Especially if he doesn't get on across the next two games.

Sports.title: Inside Erling Haaland's $10k Texas shopping spree: Shots of bourbon, line dancing... and the truth behind that $750 raccoon
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland dropped $10,000 on cowboy gear and Texas souvenirs during his first World Cup adventure in the United States, while Norway staff enjoyed shots of bourbon and line dancing lessons on their visit to one of Dallas' most iconic western stores.

The Manchester City striker captured the hearts of soccer fans across America as he led Norway to the quarterfinals in the nation's first World Cup appearance this century.

Haaland flew home after Norway's 2-1 loss against England but not before cementing his status as a superstar in the US - and splashing out on keepsakes from his travels around America.

Midway through the tournament, the striker was one of several Norway players and staff members who enjoyed a private shopping spree at Wild Bill's Western Store in Dallas. It has long been a 'common stop' for celebrities such as Chuck Norris and Arnold Schwarzenegger but co-owner Julie Newport told the Daily Mail: 'We had no idea what to expect [from Haaland and Co].'

The group stocked up on cowboy boots, western shirts, hip flasks, belt, buckles and cowboy hats. Together they racked up a bill of $10,000 before Haaland paid for it all. 'Someone needs to,' he said in a YouTube vlog of their day out.

Haaland alone bought a t-shirt which read 'Y'all can kiss my Dallas' as well as four cowboy hats - three for winter, one for summer - with at least one branded with the logo 'EH9'. 'I need a good hat,' he told staff.

Erling Haaland reportedly spent $10,000 on cowboy gear and Texas souvenirs at World Cup

He also spent $900 on a couple of stuffed squirrels, one of which is wearing a sheriff's hat

Stale Solbakken's players went viral for their 'Viking Row' celebrations during the World Cup

The striker was also given a crash course in how to store them. He learned to keep hats upside down so they don't lose their shape or their special powers.

'The superstition says: "You keep your luck in your hat,"' a staff member explained before placing the hat down on the table, brim down. 'So if I put my hat this way, my luck runs out.' He also learned how to remove his hat as a greeting to passers-by.

Haaland was joined by Norway security staff, equipment managers and teammates, who all took the chance to buy some souvenirs.

'It was so fun to see them all having such a great time,' said Newport, who shut the store doors to stop Haaland and Co being hassled. 'I gave the kit crew shots of bourbon in these little boot shot glasses, and they were just having a blast. Erling said: "I'll take a water.”'

The kitmen also enjoyed a lesson in line dancing, while Haaland later stocked up on cowboy boots after joking with staff: 'Do you have any Nike ones?'

Perhaps his most eye-catching souvenir, however, was a selection of stuffed animals. Haaland bought a taxidermy raccoon holding a bottle of liquor which cost $750. He also splashed out $900 on a couple of stuffed squirrels, one of which is wearing a sheriff's hat, while the other is leaning over a can of Budweiser.

On Monday night, Haaland was pictured stepping off the plane with the raccoon under his arm. 'It followed me home,' the Norway striker wrote alongside the photo on social media.

Since Haaland's visit, Wild Bill's has struggled to keep up with demand for his new t-shirt, while the store has now sold out of squirrels. They typically stock squirrels with a cigarette in their mouth and one 'stripper squirrel' hanging on to a pole.

The Norway superstar is seen handing a signed jersey to rapper Travis Scott

Haaland attended the Stanley Cup Finals between the Hurricanes and the Golden Knights

He also took a sightseeing tour around New York with his girlfriend Isabel Haugseng Johansen

The store ordered in a new raccoon - this one holding a wine bottle - but that sold almost immediately. Three more are being shipped in but Wild Bill's is on the hunt for a taxidermist to meet all the demand.

'I've had so many requests now for these raccoons, so I'm just telling everybody to check back next week,' Newport told the Daily Mail.

Haaland stopped by just a few hours after Norway beat Ivory Coast 2-1 in the round of 32. He had scored a late goal to seal victory and then spent another 90 minutes shopping.

'I'm honored that he took a piece of Dallas home with him,' Newport said. 'They were fun loving... [Haaland] was very approachable… there was no air about him.' The striker signed soccer balls, posters and hats while at the store.

Midfielder Sander Berge, meanwhile, bought a personalized 'El Presidente' hat that was branded with his initials and jersey number.

'I'm having the time of my life in between the games and then you're playing the most enjoyable games of football ever,' Berge said.

'Family and friends are here, what a group to do it with and everyone at home rooting for us. It's special... I think we're peaking in life... it's all downhill from here.'

The shopping spree capped a remarkable few weeks for Haaland and Norwegian football. Along with their fans, Stale Solbakken's players went viral for their 'Viking Row' celebrations on the field and in the stands.

Haaland also made the most of his time in the United States. He hung out with rapper Travis Scott, attended Game 5 of the Stanley Cup Finals between the Carolina Hurricanes and the Vegas Golden Knights, and took a sightseeing tour around New York with his girlfriend Isabel Haugseng Johansen.

Haaland at Katz's Delicatessen, the iconic New York deli known for its pastrami sandwiches

The striker racked up seven goals and one assist as Norway enjoyed its best World Cup ever

While in the Big Apple, the Manchester City star visited Times Square and Katz's Delicatessen, the iconic deli known for its giant pastrami sandwiches. Shortly before the World Cup kicked off, he enjoyed a pit stop in Monaco for the Formula 1 Grand Prix. Spider-Man star Tom Holland was also there and the actor dropped Haaland a message to try and meet up. The striker didn't even reply.

After landing in the US, meanwhile, the striker shone on the field. He racked up seven goals and one assist as Norway enjoyed its best World Cup ever. He carried the hopes of his nation and before the tournament Haaland told the Daily Mail: 'It's pressure, of course, but I like that.

It was Norway's first World Cup appearance since 1998. 'We've not been there for a long time so to have the chance to represent your country at a World Cup is special,' Haaland added.

'That's what you want as a player. People expect things from us and from me. That's normal. I just focus on my job and try to deliver.'

Sports.title: FIFA has instructed what must be shown on TV in World Cup semis and final
Sports.content:
FIFA has instructed what must be shown on TV in World Cup semis and final

The FIFA 2026 World Cup has been a star-studded event, with celebrity attendees and officials — including Gianni Infantino — deliberately shown on camera at every match

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino has regularly attended matches at the World Cup (Image: Alex Gottschalk/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

Broadcast rules at the World Cup require celebrities and FIFA officials, including president Gianni Infantino, to be shown during matches at this summer’s tournament. The semi-finals are scheduled to take place this week, with France taking on Spain in the first fixture, where a place in Sunday’s final is up for grabs.

England and Argentina will then go head-to-head in the last semi-final, with both teams meeting for the first time in a competitive fixture since the 2002 World Cup.

North America has hosted this summer’s World Cup and has seen plenty of celebrities and famous faces in attendance at matches.

The United States, Canada and Mexico have all co-hosted the tournament, and it seems the amount of attention that match-going celebrities have received has caught the eye.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

Sunday's showpiece final takes place at MetLife Stadium, where President Donald Trump is expected to play a prominent role.

The tournament has been surrounded by controversy, both on and off the pitch. From the United States' handling of Iran's squad, which forced them to relocate their training base to Tijuana, Mexico, to USMNT star Folarin Balogun's red card being rescinded following Trump's intervention, through to costly VAR errors in pivotal matches.

While Trump has yet to set foot inside a World Cup venue, having snubbed the USMNT's run to the Round of 16, one figure has been an ever-present fixture throughout: FIFA President Infantino.

It has been reported that Infantino has clocked up more than 50,000 km in the tournament's opening weeks, jetting between venues to watch matches — sometimes several in a single day.

Infantino has frequently appeared on camera, afforded the celebrity treatment typically reserved for the likes of football icon David Beckham and Hollywood star Brad Pitt.

View 2 Images David Beckham was in attendance for England's win over Norway (Image: GSI/Icon Sport via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

It has now emerged that FIFA deliberately features Infantino, FIFA World Cup officials, and celebrities on screen, despite some dissatisfaction among fans.

“It is standard practice for seats which include football officials, public figures and celebrities to be shown as part of the match running order, whoever they may be,” a FIFA spokesperson told The Athletic.

Infantino's prominence on the world stage has taken on greater significance following his confirmation that he intends to seek a third term as FIFA president in 2027.

Should he be re-elected, he would remain at the helm until 2031, extending his reign over football's global governing body to 15 years.

For now, no challenger has entered the race to oppose Infantino's bid for another term, leaving him uncontested despite the many controversies that have overshadowed his presidency.

Three of FIFA's six continental confederations — representing Africa, Asia, and South America — have already pledged their support to Infantino.

Combined, those regions account for 110 of FIFA's 211 member associations, with all three confederations unanimously backing his re-election campaign.

Sports.title: Dan Burn reveals text message to gutted Norway star after 'disrespectful' viral moment
Sports.content:
Dan Burn reveals text message to gutted Norway star after 'disrespectful' viral moment

Newcastle defender Dan Burn has quickly assumed 'cult hero' status within the England squad after back-to-back impressive cameos helped seal their World Cup semi-final berth

View 2 Images Dan Burn left Leo Ostigard in a heap at the end of England's win over Norway

Dan Burn has revealed he texted Leo Ostigard after leaving the Norway defender in a heap in Miami.

‌



Burn overpowered his former Brighton team-mate in a late aerial duel before stepping over the 26-year-old and revving up the fans. Once the adrenaline subsided, the humble Newcastle centre-back started to feel bad.

‌



He explained: "I was in a bit of my own world, to be honest. I’ve seen the video back and I used to play with Leo, the guy who I end up clattering with the header.

‌



"I didn't really know what I'd done in the moment. I watched back and I thought, ‘Oh, it's not great,’ so I texted Leo after and just said, ‘Mate, I didn't mean to be disrespectful. I was just like fired up,’ and he was like, ‘Yeah, I get that, it’s no problem.’

"When that ball's in the air, my like my eyes lit up a little bit and I just wanted to go for it and do my part for the team."

Newcastle's Toon Army love to chant about opponents "never, ever" being able to "beat Dan Burn" to the sound of Ultrabeat hit Pretty Green Eyes. He does not have an England song just yet but he has gone viral and is rapidly approaching 500k Instagram followers.

‌



Burn replied when quizzed on whether he's aware of his online cult hero status: "No, not really. I'm not massive on [using] social media, so I don't see loads of it, but I've had lots of people sending us different videos.

"For me, it's just trying to help the lads out as much as possible, and trying to make an impact on the pitch."

View 2 Images Burn has played a huge role during England's run to the World Cup semi-final

‌



World Cup 2026 news in your inbox with our Make Football Great Again newsletter

And he will hope to have another massive impact against Argentina, the opponents when he can first remember falling in love with football.

The towering 34-year-old defender was perched at a Florida bar watching national icon David Beckham blast home the all-important winner from the penalty spot in Sapporo 28 years ago.

‌



Now, in what stretches far beyond a full circle moment, Beckham is simply in awe of Burn's heroic contributions at this World Cup - just like the rest of the country.

The latter said when reflecting on England's 2002 scalp over their semi-final opponents: "I was 10. I know exactly where I was, I was in a bar called the Cricketers Arms in Orlando because we were on holiday, and it must have been on quite late because I think it was just me and my dad.

‌



"So my dad used to take us to the pub and I remember when the penalty went in, just like the roar from inside. I think that was the sort of time when I fell in love with football.

"I've said it before, like him scoring that free-kick against Greece was the first time I was like, ‘football's class’.

"I rarely get star struck now, I feel like when I meet people, I'm normally pretty cool but this time, I was like, ‘f*** me, that’s David Beckham!'"

Sports.title: Man Utd complete £35m Youri Tielemans transfer from Aston Villa as rebuild continues
Sports.content:
Man Utd complete £35m Youri Tielemans transfer from Aston Villa as rebuild continues

Youri Tielemans has joined Manchester United on a permanent deal from Aston Villa after his £35m release clause was activated

View 3 Images Youri Tielemans (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Manchester United have completed the signing of Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa. Tielemans emerged as a target for United on Monday as the Red Devils swooped in to try and bring the Belgium international to Old Trafford.

‌



Michael Carrick's side agreed to pay the £35million release clause in Tielemans’ contract, with the 29-year-old becoming the second signing of the summer, following the arrival of Andrey Santos. The Red Devils also recently agreed a deal to sign the Chelsea ace after a £50million package was finalised.

‌



United have been forced to enter the market for new midfielders following the departure of Casemiro, who left Old Trafford at the end of last month as a free agent following the expiration of his contract, and the knee injury Manuel Ugarte suffered at the World Cup.

‌



West Ham fans get clearest Jarrod Bowen update yet of where captain's future lies READ MORE :

Tielemans becomes the second new addition to Carrick’s squad this summer. After the move was confirmed, Tielemans told the official United website: "It’s hard to describe just how proud I am to join Manchester United.

"Signing for such a special club feels incredible, it is the culmination of years of dedication since I first fell in love with football. I have had the privilege of experiencing success in the game and it has only increased my determination to achieve more.

"The ambition from everyone at the club is extremely clear; we are all determined to push for the biggest trophies over the coming years.”

‌



View 3 Images Youri Tielemans has joined Manchester United (Image: Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images)

The 29-year-old was recently with the Belgium squad for this summer’s World Cup, where he scored two goals as he helped his country reach the quarter-final of the tournament.

Now that Tielemans has been signed, attention will now turn towards what other business United could conduct before the transfer window draws to a close. Atalanta star Ederson continues to be linked with a move to United and the Brazilian’s future remains uncertain after the Red Devils completed the signings of Santos and Tielemans.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jason Wilcox, director of football for the club, also said: “Youri has consistently been one of the most outstanding midfielders in the Premier League throughout the past seven years. He has all of the technical qualities, as well as the ambition and mentality, to thrive at Manchester United.

“Youri’s consistency is exceptional, and he will add further composure, creativity and leadership to our squad. We are delighted to welcome a player of his influence and experience, both on the pitch and within the dressing room, as we continue to build a team ready to challenge for the biggest honours."

‌



An initial fee worth £35million plus a further £3.8million was agreed between both clubs, and it has been reported that the move is no longer expected to be completed, but could be revisited towards the end of the transfer window. However, they are still expected to sign a new midfielder.

View 3 Images Manchester United are keen on Aurelien Tchouameni (Image: Getty Images)

Aurelien Tchouameni of France and Real Madrid continues to be a target. England international and Bournemouth ace Alex Scott has also been linked, but the Cherries are understood to be unwilling to sell the ex-Bristol City ace.

Article continues below

United will now continue their preparations for the start of the new campaign, which will see them travel to the MKM Stadium to face newly-promoted Hull City on August 22.

Sports.title: Argentina star’s mum explains why she refuses to sing anti-England songs after u-turn
Sports.content:
Argentina star’s mum explains why she refuses to sing anti-England songs after u-turn

Argentina and England resume their bitter rivalry in the World Cup semi-finals on Wednesday but Alexis Mac Allister’s mum will not be joining in with any anti-Three Lions chants

View 2 Images Alexis Mac Allister has been key to Argentina's run to the World Cup semi-finals (Image: Getty Images)

Alexis Mac Allister’s mum will refuse to join in with any anti-England chants at the World Cup due to her UK-born granddaughter. The Three Lions will take on Argentina in the semi finals on Wednesday evening in what is the latest chapter in a long-running international rivalry.

‌



Argentina players have already been spotted singing about the Falkland Islands ahead of the game, while some supporters have shared video montages of the conflict on social media.

‌



And while that rivalry is expected to be fierce in Atlanta on Wednesday, one person who won’t be joining in is Mac Allister’s mum, Silvina Riela. Having previously held a negative opinion of England, she has completely changed her mind following the midfielder’s spells with Brighton and Liverpool.

‌



“I had a rather negative impression of England, at least regarding living there, due to the cold and the lack of sunshine. In my ignorance, I used to say, ‘I hope we never end up in England,’” she told Buenos Aires' Radio Mitre.

England vs Argentina World Cup clash can spark Falklands ‘fire’ warns BBC presenter READ MORE :

FIFA told they have made mistake with choice of referee for England vs Argentina READ MORE :

“But now that I've experienced it, everything has changed, even the way I see the people. I expected to encounter cold, distant people, but they are actually very polite and respectful. We were welcomed by a country that has treated us in the best possible way.”

Meanwhile, she has also confirmed that her English-born granddaughter is the main reason why she doesn’t join in with any chants against the country. She added: “There is that situation involving England, stemming somewhat from the history regarding the Malvinas Islands. As (Argentina manager Lionel) Scaloni said, it's just a football match.

‌



“My granddaughter was born in England. So, when everyone sings, ‘Whoever doesn't jump is English,’ I stay seated with her. I can't join in on that; I don't participate in that part.”

Mac Allister, 27, has once again been key in Argentina’s run to the semi finals in the USA, Mexico and Canada, the Liverpool midfielder having started every game but one. He also got the South American side off to the perfect start with a goal in their quarter-final win against Switzerland.

View 2 Images Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister and mother, Silvina Riela (Image: silvinarie/Instagram)

‌



He has also spoken out on the upcoming game. Mac Allsiter said: “We understand the context behind it, all the rivalry stemming from past events and history.

“Obviously, we also realise that this isn't the fault of their people or ours, but rather those in positions of power, so we shouldn't conflate the two.

“I have a lot of respect for (England); I've been there for six years now, and they've always treated me incredibly well. From a footballing perspective, there's no doubt they want to beat us at all costs, and it's going to be a very tough match.

Article continues below

“So now, the task is to prepare the best we can; while there is mutual respect, it's going to be a great battle out on the pitch.”

Sports.title: Man Utd eye three more transfers after £85m deals are confirmed
Sports.content:
Man Utd eye three more transfers after £85m deals are confirmed

Manchester United have been busy in the transfer market this summer and are reportedly planning to sign at least three more players before the window closes

View 2 Images Manchester United could have a busy end to the summer transfer window

Manchester United’s plans for the rest of the summer transfer window have emerged, a day after wrapping up two deals. United are expected to have a busy few weeks in the transfer market as they look to strengthen their squad ahead of next season.

‌



Monday saw Andrey Santos become United's first official signing of the summer transfer window, with the Reds agreeing a £50million deal with Chelsea for the Brazilian to move to Old Trafford.

‌



Karl Darlow has also signed for United on a free transfer just a couple of weeks after his contract at Leeds United ran out.

‌



Aston Villa star Youri Tielemans has emerged as a target for United this summer, with the Belgium international thought to have a £35million release clause in his contract at Villa Park.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

BBC star admits referee and VAR concerns for England's World Cup showdown with Argentina READ MORE :

England vs Argentina World Cup clash can spark Falklands ‘fire’ warns BBC presenter READ MORE :

The update regarding Tielemans comes amidst uncertainty surrounding the future of Atalanta star Ederson, whom United had previously agreed to sign earlier in the summer for £35million plus an additional £3.8million in add-ons.

‌



However, Atalanta director Cristiano Giuntoli has today stated: "We were stunned [by Man United calling Ederson deal off]. Now we are working on a new contract for him."

Michael Carrick will be occupied preparing his squad for the beginning of the new Premier League season, with pre-season commencing later this week.

With the summer transfer window remaining open, United are now expected to enter the market for at least three more new players.

‌



According to The Sun, United will seek to bring in another midfielder, left winger and a forward once a deal to sign Tielemans is completed. Should this come to pass, it would bring United's total number of new arrivals to six ahead of their return to Champions League football.

Nevertheless, the report also suggests that United could "pause" further incomings after wrapping up a deal for Tielemans, while they weigh up their options and push through departures from the club this summer.

View 2 Images Youri Tielemans has been linked with a move to Manchester United (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

United head to Finland this week as they take on Wrexham on Saturday in their opening pre-season friendly of the campaign, before travelling on to Norway to face Rosenborg just a few days later.

Carrick and Co. will then go up against Atletico Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain in friendly matches in Sweden, before heading to the Republic of Ireland to meet Leeds in Dublin to round off their pre-season schedule.

Article continues below

All of that will serve as the build-up to United's first fixture of the new Premier League campaign, which will see them take on newly-promoted Hull City at the MKM Stadium on Saturday, August 22.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino now 'facing fight to remain FIFA president' after World Cup controversies
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino now 'facing fight to remain FIFA president' after World Cup controversies

The action on the pitch at the World Cup has been exciting, but it appears FIFA boss Gianni Infantino still has plenty of dissenters

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino's future as FIFA president may not be as secure as first thought (Image: Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/Shutterstock)

FIFA president Gianni Infantino may be facing a fight to hold onto his presidency at the governing body of global football. Infantino was elected in 2016, where he replaced the disgraced Sepp Blatter, who was banned from football for eight years by the body's Ethics Committee amid the corruption scandal that shook the game.

‌



Infantino is now seeking a third term at next April's FIFA congress, which was long expected to be a formality for the Swiss figurehead, with no contenders expected to challenge him. However, new reports have claimed Infantino could be contested after a World Cup dogged by controversy.

‌



The most significant of the issues was Folarin Balogun's red card being suspended for a year, not long after US president Donald Trump contacted Infantino and urged him to review the incident. In the wake of this, Infantino's next election may not be a procession, as first thought.

‌



Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

According to talkSPORT, members within UEFA are willing to support candidates to challenge Infantino. Current president of UEFA Alexander Ceferin is not the one who will do so, as he is looking to remain in his current role.

PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi was also somebody put forward, but he also does not have any ambition to challenge Infantino. However, it's been claimed Legia Warsaw owner Dariusz Mioduski would command support from Bosnian, Norwegian, Swedish, German and Spanish officials, if he was to stake claim to take over FIFA.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Meanwhile, CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani has been touted as a potential contender, with the Canadian purported to have aspirations of one day taking charge of the governing body. FIFA's current constitution currently dictates a president cannot stand for a fourth time, meaning Infantino's reign is set to end in 2031.

Infantino does still command many allies, particularly within the smaller nations hoping to compete in the World Cup. His recent suggestion to expand the World Cup to 64 teams will also chime well with those associates, who would not want to jeopardise the expansion by voting him out.

‌



View 3 Images Infantino also rallied to create the FIFA Peace Price which was then given to Donald Trump (Image: AP)

However, there is still anger about the situation around Balogun. Infantino claimed an independent disciplinary committee chose to suspend the one-match suspension for one year, allowing Balogun to play in the USA's round of 16 clash against Belgium.

FIFA pointed to Article 27 of the FIFA Disciplinary Code, which states "The judicial body may decide to fully or partially suspend the implementation of a disciplinary measure.”

‌



View 3 Images The following events after Balogun's red card have been controversial (Image: AP Photo/Julio Cortez)

However, The Times have since claimed that the controversial call was made solely by one official - Mohammad al-Kamali, the chairman of FIFA's disciplinary committee. He reportedly did so without consulting any of the other 17 members.

A complaint has also been launched to the International Olympic Committee by human rights organisation FairSquare, claiming Infantino breached the Olympic Charter and the IOC's code of ethics throughout the Balogun saga.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
